title: Synthetic burst sampler for differential regression detection in PR gating
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Goal: Add a lightweight synthetic burst sampling harness to PR CI that reproduces realistic microbursts and short steady-state windows, enabling differential comparison against a rolling baseline to detect subtle p95 and tokens/sec regressions before merging.

Why: Current CI smoke runs capture steady throughput but miss short lived microburst behavior that causes latency spikes in production (observed during week-long incidents). We need a repeatable, fast, low-cost test that surfaces regressions in request handling, batching, and kernel scheduling that manifest only under short bursts.

Approach:
- Implement a sampler that composes short sequences of traffic patterns: single-request spikes (1s, 5s), bursty floods (10–50 concurrent simulated requests for 3–7s), and short ramp-ups. Each run lasts ~90s and emits token-level traces plus server-side metrics.
- Use a rolling baseline stored in S3 (compact fingerprint: p50/p95/tokens_per_sec distributions, warm-up profile) aggregated from last N successful CI runs on main.
- Compare PR run to baseline using a Bayesian difference estimator and an ordinal bootstrap for p95 to produce probabilistic regression signals (e.g., probability p95 increased > 10% > 95% posterior probability).
- Integrate as an optional stage in PR workflows: baseline-local runs for forks disabled, PRs on main branches run sampler in parallel with existing smoke checks; failures produce a human-readable regression report and block merge if posteriority > threshold.
- Instrument traces for KV cache hit/miss, batch sizes, queue delays, and CPU/GPU utilization to aid root cause.

Acceptance criteria:
- Sampler job completes in < 3 minutes with < 20% additional cost compared to current smoke test.
- Regression detection produces clear pass/fail with probability score and links to artifact traces/dashboards.
- False positive rate on historical PRs (retrospective run) < 5% at configured threshold for detectable regressions.
- On known regressions from incident-logs, sampler consistently flags the change.

Implementation plan:
1) Prototype sampler as a test harness in repo redwood/perf-ci (synth_burst.py) and a canonical job spec for k8s runner.
2) Add lightweight aggregator to compute rolling baseline summaries and verification job to refresh baseline daily.
3) Implement statistical comparator library (py) with tunable thresholds and output schema.
4) CI integration: add workflow file and gating logic (blocker flag) guarded behind feature flag rollout.
5) Dashboards: new perf-ci page with recent sampler runs, baseline history, and PR-level comparisons.

Risks & mitigations:
- Noise from infra variability: mitigate via paired-run comparison (run baseline and PR against same commit where possible) and multiple repeats per PR.
- Cost: limit sampler to run only on PRs that change runtime or core infra files (codeowners pattern) or when label "perf-check" is present.
- Flaky signal: include auto-retry and minimum sample size policy; in borderline cases report for human triage rather than blocking.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0: internal prototype run by oncall and performance team for 2 weeks.
- Phase 1: enable on PRs touching runtime surface area with non-blocking annotation.
- Phase 2: promote to blocking gate for critical repos after 4 weeks and low FP measured.
